correctness.rationale: Exact inversion of the symmetric three-node Gaussian kernel matrix yields the weight formulas given in RESULT.md. Endpoint positivity is an integral of a strictly positive hyperbolic-cosine excess. The sign of the center weight is the sign of a positive-inner minus positive-outer integral. For every pair of inner and outer integration points, the logarithmic time derivative of their positive integrand ratio is strictly positive: its proof uses a hyperbolic-cotangent auxiliary function with derivative strictly between zero and one. Integrating cross-products proves that the ratio of the two integrals is strictly increasing. The flat-kernel comparison has the exact node-radius boundary proved in RESULT.md, and the center weight is eventually positive by exponentially vanishing kernel cross-correlation. These facts prove the entire sign classification and uniqueness of the crossing. The nonnegative-polynomial witness proves an actual positivity defect. An independent arbitrary-precision matrix linear-solve verifier passed 389 finite checks, not used as a substitute for analytic proof.

value.rationale: Positivity of kernel quadrature is a mathematically motivated stability requirement; unlike a trivial flat-limit computation, the result gives a complete necessary-and-sufficient geometry/shape positivity phase diagram for a natural three-node Gaussian RBF rule, with a strict one-crossing proof and an explicit smooth positive-input counterexample. It explains when changing kernel scale alone can restore positivity on fixed nodes, and when all scales are safe. This finite model is a sharp reproducible benchmark for shape tuning and kernel-quadrature design; no unsupported larger-dimensional extension is asserted.
